sentences.zh: 李乂李乂，本名尚真，趙州房子人也。

translations.literal: Li Yi—Li Yi, original personal name Shangzhen, was a native of Fangzi in Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, whose original name was Shangzhen, came from Fangzi in Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少與兄尚一、尚貞俱以文章見稱，舉進士。

translations.literal: In youth he and his elder brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were all famed for literary talent and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he and his brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were all celebrated for their writing and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he rose through successive appointments to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時中宗遣使江南分道贖生，以所在官物充直。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhongzong sent envoys to Jiangnan by separate routes to ransom living creatures for release, using official goods from each locality as payment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Zhongzong dispatched envoys to the Jiangnan region by separate routes to buy captive animals for release, paying with official goods held in each district.

sentences.zh: 乂上疏曰：「江南水鄉，采捕為業，魚鱉之利，黎元所資，土地使然，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial saying: "The Jiangnan region is a land of rivers and lakes; hunting and fishing are its livelihood. The profit of fish and turtles is what the common people rely on for support. The land makes this so, and it has been so from of old."
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial that read: "Jiangnan is a country of waterways; gathering and fishing are its trades. Fish and turtles are what the people live on—the land has made it so since long ago."

sentences.zh: 伏以聖慈含育，恩周動植，布天下之大德，及鱗介之微品。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your sagely compassion nourishes and bears all things, extending grace to both moving and rooted life, spreading the great virtue of the empire even to the smallest scaly and shelled creatures.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty's sacred kindness nurtures all life, extending favor to every plant and animal, spreading imperial virtue even to the tiniest fish and shellfish.

sentences.zh: 雖雲雨之私，有霑於末類；

translations.literal: Though the private favor of cloud and rain may reach the lowliest kinds;
translations.idiomatic: Though the gentle rain of grace may touch even the humblest creatures;

sentences.zh: 而生成之惠，未洽於平人。

translations.literal: the bounty of sustaining life has not yet fully reached ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: the blessing of nurturing life has not yet fully reached the common people.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 江湖之饒，生育無限；

translations.literal: The abundance of rivers and lakes breeds without limit;
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and lakes teem with life beyond measure;

sentences.zh: 府庫之用，支供易殫。

translations.literal: the expenditures of the treasury are easily exhausted in supplying them.
translations.idiomatic: yet treasury outlays to support the policy are quickly spent dry.

sentences.zh: 費之若少，則所濟何成；

translations.literal: if the expense is small, then what is accomplished by the relief?
translations.idiomatic: If the expense is modest, little is actually saved;

sentences.zh: 用之倘多，則常支有闕。

translations.literal: if the use is large, then the regular outlays will fall short.
translations.idiomatic: if it is large, the ordinary budget will fall short.

sentences.zh: 在於拯物，豈若憂人。

translations.literal: When it comes to saving creatures, how does that compare to caring for people?
translations.idiomatic: To rescue animals—how can that compare with relieving human distress?

sentences.zh: 且鬻生之徒，唯利斯視，錢刀日至，網罟年滋，施之一朝，營之百倍，未若回救贖之錢物，減困貧之徭賦，活國愛人，其福勝彼。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who sell living things look only to profit; coins arrive daily and nets increase year by year. A single day's expenditure yields a hundredfold return. Better to turn back the funds used for ransoming and reduce corvée and taxes burdening the poor and distressed—saving the state and loving the people brings greater blessing than that.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sellers of captive animals care only for profit: money flows in every day and nets multiply year by year. One day's outlay from the court yields a hundredfold in their trade. Far better to divert the ransom funds and lighten levies on the poor—reviving the state and cherishing the people would bring a greater blessing still."

sentences.zh: 乂知制誥凡數載。

translations.literal: Yi drafted imperial edicts for several years in all.
translations.idiomatic: For several years Yi served as drafter of imperial proclamations.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，遷吏部侍郎，與宋璟、盧從願同時典選，銓敘平允，甚為當時所稱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; together with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan he concurrently managed selection, conducting appointments with fairness, and was greatly praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 he became Vice Minister of Personnel. He shared charge of appointments with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan, and their even-handed evaluations won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 尋轉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗令造金仙、玉真二觀，乂頻上疏諫，帝每優容之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ruizong ordered construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries; Yi repeatedly submitted memorials in remonstrance, and the emperor each time treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ordered the building of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries, Yi memorialized repeatedly in protest, and the emperor each time received him leniently.

sentences.zh: 開元初，特令乂與中書侍郎蘇颋纂集起居註，錄其嘉謨昌言可體國經遠者，別編奏之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was specially ordered, together with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Ting, to compile the Diaries of Activity and Repose, selecting excellent plans and splendid words fit to embody statecraft and guide the distant future, editing them separately and submitting them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he was specially assigned, with Secretariat Vice Minister Su Ting, to compile the court diaries, extract counsel and speeches that could serve long-range statecraft, and present them in a separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 乂在門下，多所駁正。

translations.literal: While Yi served in the Chancellery, he often rejected and corrected documents.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Chancellery, Yi frequently struck down or revised draft documents.

sentences.zh: 開元初，姚崇為紫微令，薦乂為紫微侍郎，外托薦賢，其實引在己下，去其糾駁之權也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan Yao Chong was Director of the Purple Tenuity Bureau; he recommended Yi as Vice Director, outwardly on the pretext of promoting the worthy, but in fact drawing him beneath himself and removing his power to criticize and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, when Yao Chong headed the Purple Tenuity Bureau, he recommended Yi as vice director—ostensibly to advance talent, but in truth to place him under his own authority and strip him of the power to review and reject.

sentences.zh: 俄拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 乂方雅有學識，朝廷稱其有宰相之望，會病卒。

translations.literal: Yi was refined and possessed learning; the court said he had the makings of a chief minister, but he happened to die of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and learned, Yi was spoken of at court as a man with the makings of a chief minister, but he died of illness before that could come to pass.

sentences.zh: 兄尚一，清源尉，早卒；

translations.literal: His elder brother Shangyi, magistrate of Qingyuan, died early;
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shangyi, magistrate of Qingyuan, died young;

sentences.zh: 尚貞，官至博州刺史。

translations.literal: Shangzhen rose to governor of Bo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhen rose to serve as governor of Bo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同為一集，號曰《李氏花萼集》，總二十卷。

translations.literal: The brothers jointly compiled one collection, entitled Collected Writings of the Li Brothers at the Flower Calyx Pavilion, twenty juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers jointly published a collection called the Li Brothers' Flower Calyx Anthology, twenty juan in all.

sentences.zh: 薛登薛登，本名謙光，常州義興人也。

translations.literal: Xue Deng—Xue Deng, original personal name Qian'guang, was a native of Yixing in Chang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Deng, whose original name was Qian'guang, came from Yixing in Chang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父士通，大業中為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: His father Shitong served as General of Soaring Hawks during the Daye reign.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shitong was a General of Soaring Hawks in the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 江都之亂，士通與鄉人聞人嗣安等同據本郡，以禦寇賊。

translations.literal: During the turmoil at Jiangdu, Shitong together with his fellow townsman Wenren Sian and others jointly held their home commandery to repel bandits and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos engulfed Jiangdu, Shitong joined his countryman Wenren Sian and others in holding their home commandery against marauders.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，遣使歸國，高祖嘉之，降璽書勞勉，拜東武州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he sent envoys to submit to the dynasty; Emperor Gaozu commended him, issued an imperial letter of commendation and encouragement, and appointed him governor of Dongwu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 he sent envoys to pledge allegiance. Emperor Gaozu praised him, sent an imperial letter of encouragement, and appointed him governor of Dongwu.

sentences.zh: 俄而輔公祏於江都構逆，遣其將西門君儀等寇常州，士通率兵拒戰，大破之，君儀等僅以身免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Fu Gongshi rebelled at Jiangdu and sent his generals Ximen Junyi and others to raid Chang prefecture; Shitong led troops to resist, inflicted a great defeat, and Junyi and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fu Gongshi rose in rebellion at Jiangdu and sent generals such as Ximen Junyi against Chang. Shitong met them in battle, routed them utterly, and Junyi's party escaped only with their lives.

sentences.zh: 及公祏平，累功封臨汾侯。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was pacified, Shitong's accumulated merit earned him enfeoffment as Marquis of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongshi's defeat, his accumulated merit won him the title Marquis of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷遷泉州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was promoted in succession to governor of Quan prefecture and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he rose to governor of Quan prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 謙光博涉文史，每與人談論前代故事，必廣引證驗，有如目擊。

translations.literal: Qian'guang was broadly versed in literature and history; whenever he discussed stories of former ages with others, he invariably cited wide proofs and verification, as though he had seen them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qian'guang was widely read in letters and history. When he discussed events of earlier times, he cited evidence so fully that he seemed to have witnessed them himself.

sentences.zh: 少與徐堅、劉子玄齊名友善。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed on equal terms with Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan and was on friendly terms with them.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he ranked with Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan in reputation and counted them among his close friends.

sentences.zh: 文明中，解褐閬中主簿。

translations.literal: During the Wenming era he left the commoner's garb and was appointed chief clerk of Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During Wenming he entered official service as chief clerk of Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 天授中，為左補闕，時選舉頗濫，謙光上疏曰：

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he served as Left Remonstrator; at that time appointments were quite lax, and Qian'guang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou period he became Left Remonstrator. Appointments had grown lax, and Qian'guang submitted a memorial that began:

sentences.zh: 尋轉水部員外郎，累遷給事中、檢校常州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works for Water Control; he rose in succession to Supervising Secretary and acting governor of Chang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director in the Ministry of Works' water bureau, then rose to Supervising Secretary and acting governor of Chang.

sentences.zh: 屬宣州狂寇硃大目作亂，百姓奔走，謙光嚴備安輯，闔境肅然。

translations.literal: When the mad bandit Zhu Damu of Xuan prefecture rose in rebellion and the people fled in panic, Qian'guang made strict preparations, pacified and settled the region, and the whole jurisdiction became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Zhu Damu of Xuanzhou threw the region into turmoil and the people scattered in panic, Qian'guang tightened defenses, restored order, and the whole circuit grew calm.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，再遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, granted the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and was again promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Justice, received the Silver-Green Tally grand master title, and was later promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，擢拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era he was promoted and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun period he was elevated to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時僧惠範恃太平公主權勢，逼奪百姓店肆，州縣不能理。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Huifan relied on the power of Princess Taiping and forcibly seized shops from common people; the prefectures and counties could not deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huifan, backed by Princess Taiping's influence, seized commoners' shops by force, and local officials could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 謙光將加彈奏，或請寢之，謙光曰：「憲臺理冤滯，何所回避，朝彈暮黜，亦可矣。

translations.literal: Qian'guang was about to impeach him; some asked that the matter be dropped. Qian'guang said: "The Censorate exists to redress wrongs and delays—what is there to avoid? To be impeached in the morning and dismissed in the evening would be enough."
translations.idiomatic: Qian'guang prepared to impeach him, but others urged him to let the matter drop. He said: "The Censorate exists to clear injustice—why should I shrink back? If I am impeached at dawn and dismissed at dusk, so be it."

sentences.zh: 」遂與殿中慕容玽奏彈之，反為太平公主所構，出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: " He then joined Palace Censor Murong Ting in submitting an impeachment, but was instead framed by Princess Taiping and sent out as governor of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He and Palace Censor Murong Ting then jointly impeached Huifan, but Princess Taiping framed him instead, and he was demoted to governor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 惠範既誅，遷太子賓客，轉刑部尚書，加金紫光祿大夫、昭文館學士。

translations.literal: After Huifan was executed, Qian'guang was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Minister of Justice, and granted the additional titles Grand Master with Gold-Purple Tally and Academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Huifan was put to death, he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Minister of Justice, with the Gold-Purple Tally title and a post as Zhaowen Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為東都留守，又轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as Defender of the Eastern Capital, then was again transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he served as Defender of the Eastern Capital, then returned to the post of Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以與太子同名，表請行字，特敕賜名登。

translations.literal: Because he shared the heir apparent's personal name, he submitted a memorial requesting to use his style name; by special edict he was granted the name Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Because his personal name matched the heir apparent's, he memorialized to use his style name instead, and an imperial edict specially granted him the name Deng.

sentences.zh: 尋以孽子悅千牛為憲司所劾，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because his illegitimate son Yue, a Thousand-Ox Guardsman, was impeached by the censorate, he was released to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his illegitimate son Yue, a Thousand-Ox Guardsman, was impeached by the censorate, and Deng was sent home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其家貧，又特給致仕祿。

translations.literal: Because his household was poor, the court specially granted him retirement stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his family was poor, the court also granted him a special retirement stipend.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，年七十三，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died at age seventy-three; posthumously he was made governor of Jin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year at seventy-three; posthumously he was honored as governor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 撰《四時記》二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Records of the Four Seasons in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of the Four Seasons in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 韋湊韋湊，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Cou—Wei Cou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou came from Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 曾祖瓚，隋尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zan was Right Vice Director of the Secretariat under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zan served as Sui Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖叔諧，蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuxie was governor of Pu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuxie was governor of Pu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父玄，桂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was chief administrator of the Guizhou Area Command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was chief administrator of the Guizhou military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 湊，永淳二年，解褐授婺州參軍，累轉揚府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Cou, in the second year of Yongchun, left the commoner's garb and was appointed military aide in Wu prefecture; he rose in succession to legal aide in the Yangzhou prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Cou entered service in Yongchun 2 as military aide in Wu prefecture and later became legal aide in the Yangzhou prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 州人前仁壽令孟神爽豪縱，數犯法，交通貴戚，前後官吏莫敢繩按，湊白長史張潛，請因事除之。

translations.literal: A former magistrate of Renshou in the prefecture, Meng Shenshuang, was overbearing and unrestrained, repeatedly violated the law, and had connections with noble kin; officials before and after dared not investigate him. Cou reported to Chief Administrator Zhang Qian and asked to remove him when opportunity arose.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Shenshuang, a former Renshou magistrate in the prefecture, was violent and lawless and cultivated ties with powerful families; no previous official had dared prosecute him. Cou informed Chief Administrator Zhang Qian and asked leave to bring him down when the chance came.

sentences.zh: 會神爽坐事推問，湊無所假借，神爽妄稱有密旨，究問引虛，遂杖殺之，遠近稱伏。

translations.literal: When Shenshuang was implicated in a matter and put to interrogation, Cou showed no leniency; Shenshuang falsely claimed there was a secret edict, but investigation proved the claim empty, and Cou had him beaten to death. Near and far submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenshuang was brought in for questioning, Cou showed no mercy. Shenshuang falsely claimed a secret imperial order protected him, but investigation exposed the lie, and Cou had him beaten to death. People near and far applauded.

sentences.zh: 湊，景龍中歷遷將作少匠、司農少卿。

translations.literal: Cou, during the Jinglong era, rose in succession to Vice Director of Palace Buildings and Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period Cou rose to Vice Director of Palace Buildings and Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 嘗以公事忤宗楚客，出為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Once, on official business, he offended Zong Chuke and was sent out as governor of Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He once clashed with Zong Chuke over official business and was posted out as governor of Bei.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，拜鴻臚少卿，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Cou was appointed Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies and granted the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, Cou became Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies and received the Silver-Green Tally grand master title.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，轉太府少卿，又兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and also concurrently served as Herald for Foreign Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 he became Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury and also served concurrently as Herald for Foreign Envoys.

sentences.zh: 時改葬節湣太子，優詔加謚；

translations.literal: At that time the Jiemin Crown Prince was being reburied and an edict of special favor added to his posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiemin Crown Prince was being reburied, and an edict of special favor enlarged his posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 又雪李多祚等罪，還其官爵，仍議更加贈官。

translations.literal: the crimes of Li Duozuo and others were also cleared, their offices and titles restored, and there was further discussion of adding posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: the convictions of Li Duozuo and others were cleared and their offices restored, while the court also debated further posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 湊上書曰：

translations.literal: Cou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 書奏，睿宗引湊謂曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong summoned Cou and said: "What you say is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, Emperor Ruizong summoned Cou and said, "What you say is true.

sentences.zh: 事已如此，如何改動？

translations.literal: Matters have already gone this far—how can they be changed?"
translations.idiomatic: But matters have already gone this far—how can we change them now?"

sentences.zh: 」湊曰：「太子實行悖逆，不可褒美，請稱其行，改謚以一字。

translations.literal: " Cou said: "The crown prince in fact acted in rebellion and must not be praised. I ask that his conduct be named and the posthumous title changed by a single character.
translations.idiomatic: Cou replied: "The crown prince truly committed treason and must not be praised. Name his conduct plainly and change the posthumous title by a single character.

sentences.zh: 多祚等以兵犯君，非曰無罪，只可雲放，不可稱雪。

translations.literal: Duozuo and the others took up arms against their ruler—it cannot be called innocence; one may only say they were released, not that their guilt was cleared."
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo and his fellows took up arms against their sovereign—they were not innocent. Say they were released, not that their guilt was cleared."

sentences.zh: 」帝然其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 當時執政以制令已行，難於改易，唯多祚等停贈官而已。

translations.literal: The men then in power held that the edicts had already been issued and were hard to change; only the additional posthumous honors for Duozuo and the others were halted.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power held that the edicts had already gone forth and were hard to revise; only the added posthumous honors for Duozuo and his fellows were stopped.

sentences.zh: 明年春，起金仙、玉真兩觀，用工巨億。

translations.literal: The next spring construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries was begun, employing labor on the scale of hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring work resumed on the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries at a cost of hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 湊進諫曰：「陛下去夏，以妨農停兩觀作，今正農月，翻欲興功。

translations.literal: Cou remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty last summer halted work on the two monasteries because it interfered with farming; now, in the very month of agriculture, you wish instead to raise works.
translations.idiomatic: Cou remonstrated: "Last summer Your Majesty halted the two monasteries because they harmed the harvest. Now, in the heart of the farming season, you wish to resume construction.

sentences.zh: 雖知用公主錢，不出庫物，但土木作起，高價雇人，三輔農人，趨目前之利，舍農受雇，棄本逐末。

translations.literal: Although it is known that the princess's funds are used and nothing comes from the treasury stores, once earthworks and timber construction begin, labor is hired at high wages; farmers of the three metropolitan districts, chasing immediate profit, abandon farming to take employment and forsake the root to pursue the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the princess's funds are used and nothing is drawn from the treasury, once building begins labor is hired at high wages. Farmers of the capital districts, tempted by quick pay, leave the fields for hire and abandon the essential for the trivial.

sentences.zh: 臣聞一夫不耕，天下有受其饑者，臣竊恐不可。

translations.literal: I have heard that if one man does not plow, someone in the empire will go hungry because of it—I fear this cannot be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when one man leaves the plow, someone in the realm goes hungry. I fear this cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 」帝不應。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not answer.

sentences.zh: 湊又奏曰：「日陽和布氣，萬物生育，土木之間，昆蟲無數。

translations.literal: Cou submitted again, saying: "Now the sun spreads warm harmony and all things grow; between earthworks and timber there are countless insects.
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted again: "The sun now spreads spring warmth and all things quicken. Between earth and timber countless insects teem.

sentences.zh: 此時興造，傷殺甚多，臣亦恐非仁聖本旨。

translations.literal: To raise construction at this time kills many of them—I also fear this is not the original intent of benevolent sageliness."
translations.idiomatic: Building now would kill vast numbers of them, and I fear that is not the intent of a benevolent sage-ruler."

sentences.zh: 」睿宗方納其言，令在外詳議。

translations.literal: " Only then did Emperor Ruizong accept his words and order detailed discussion outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Emperor Ruizong accept his counsel and order the matter debated further outside court.

sentences.zh: 中書令崔湜、侍中岑羲謂湊曰：「公敢言此，大是難事。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui Shi and Palace Attendant Cen Yi said to Cou: "Sir, you dared speak thus—this was a very difficult thing.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cui Shi and Palace Attendant Cen Yi told Cou, "You dared say this—that was no small feat.

sentences.zh: 」湊曰：「叨食厚祿，死且不辭，況在明時，必知不死。

translations.literal: " Cou said: "I enjoy a generous salary and would not refuse even death; moreover, in an enlightened age, I was certain I would not die."
translations.idiomatic: Cou replied, "I enjoy a generous stipend and would not refuse even death; and in an enlightened age, I knew I would not die."

sentences.zh: 」尋出為陜州刺史，無幾，轉汝州刺史。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he was sent out as governor of Shan prefecture; before long he was transferred to governor of Ru prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted out as governor of Shan, and not long after was transferred to Ru.

sentences.zh: 開元二年夏，敕靖陵建碑，征料夫匠。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Kaiyuan an edict ordered a stele erected at Jing Mausoleum and laborers and craftsmen requisitioned.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kaiyuan 2 an edict ordered a stele raised at Jing Mausoleum and laborers requisitioned.

sentences.zh: 湊以自古園陵無建碑之禮，又時正旱儉，不可興功，飛表極諫，工役乃止。

translations.literal: Cou held that from antiquity imperial tombs had no rite of erecting steles, and that at a time of drought and scarcity works could not be raised; he sent a rapid memorial in utmost remonstrance, and the labor was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Cou argued that imperial tombs had never had steles by ancient rite, and that drought and scarcity made work impossible. He sent an urgent memorial in strong protest, and the labor was stopped.

sentences.zh: 尋遷岐州剌史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to governor of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為將作大匠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered the capital as Director of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to the capital as Director of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 時有敕復孝敬廟為義宗，湊上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time an edict restored the Xiaojing Temple as the Temple of Righteous Ancestor; Cou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: An edict then restored the Xiaojing Temple under the title Temple of Righteous Ancestor. Cou submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 於是敕太常議，遂停義宗之號。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate, and the title of Righteous Ancestor was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate, and the title of Righteous Ancestor was dropped.

sentences.zh: 湊前後上書論時政得失，多見采納。

translations.literal: Cou repeatedly submitted memorials discussing the gains and losses of current policy, and many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Cou repeatedly memorialized on the strengths and failings of current policy, and many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 再遷河南尹，累封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Metropolitan Governor of Henan and was cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Metropolitan Governor of Henan and was enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以公事左授杭州刺史，轉汾州刺史。

translations.literal: On official business he was demoted to the left and appointed governor of Hang prefecture, then transferred to governor of Fen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a demotion on official grounds he became governor of Hang, then was transferred to Fen.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜太原尹兼節度支度營田大使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Taiyuan and concurrently Military Commissioner for Supplies, Expenditure, and Agricultural Colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Taiyuan and concurrently commissioner for military supplies, finance, and agricultural colonies.

sentences.zh: 其年卒官，年六十五。

translations.literal: That same year he died in office at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died in office at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Area Commander of You prefecture; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Area Commander of You, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子見素，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Jiansu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiansu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 湊從子虛心。

translations.literal: Cou's nephew was Xuxin.
translations.idiomatic: Cou's nephew was Xuxin.

sentences.zh: 湊從子 虛心虛心父維，少習儒業，博涉文史，舉進士。

translations.literal: Cou's nephew Xuxin—Xuxin's father Wei, in youth studied Confucian learning, was broadly versed in literature and history, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Cou's nephew Xuxin: Xuxin's father Wei studied Confucian learning in his youth, became widely read in letters and history, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 自大理丞累至戶部郎中，善於剖判，時員外郎宋之問工於詩，時人以為戶部有二妙。

translations.literal: From aide in the Court of Judicial Review he rose in succession to Director in the Ministry of Revenue; he was skilled in deciding cases. At the time Vice Director Song Zhiwen was accomplished in poetry, and contemporaries regarded the Ministry of Revenue as having two marvels.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from aide in the Court of Judicial Review to director in the Ministry of Revenue and excelled at deciding cases. Vice Director Song Zhiwen was celebrated for poetry, and people said the ministry had two outstanding talents.

sentences.zh: 終於左庶子。

translations.literal: He finally reached Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose at last to Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 虛心舉孝廉，為官嚴整，累至大理丞、侍御史。

translations.literal: Xuxin was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt; as an official he was strict and orderly, and rose in succession to aide in the Court of Judicial Review and palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin entered service through the Filial and Incorrupt recommendation, governed with stern discipline, and rose to aide in the Court of Judicial Review and palace censor.

sentences.zh: 神龍年，推按大獄，時僕射竇懷貞、侍中劉幽求意欲寬假，虛心堅執法令，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong years he investigated major cases; at the time Left Vice Director Dou Huaizhen and Palace Attendant Liu Youqiu wished to show leniency, but Xuxin firmly upheld the law with a will that could not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenlong he investigated major criminal cases. Left Vice Director Dou Huaizhen and Palace Attendant Liu Youqiu wished to show leniency, but Xuxin held fast to the law with unshakable resolve.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，西域羌胡背叛，時並擒獲，有敕盡欲誅之。

translations.literal: During Jinglong the Qiang and Hu of the Western Regions rebelled; at the time they were all captured, and an edict ordered that all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period Qiang and Hu of the western frontier rebelled and were captured in large numbers; an edict ordered them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 虛心論奏，但罪元首，其所全者千餘人。

translations.literal: Xuxin argued in a memorial that only the ringleaders should be punished; those he spared numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin memorialized that only the leaders should be punished, thereby sparing more than a thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 虛心有孝行，及丁父憂，哀毀過禮，鬚鬢盡白，朝廷深所嗟尚。

translations.literal: Xuxin was filial; when he entered mourning for his father, his grief exceeded the rites and his beard and hair turned entirely white; the court deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin was famed for filial piety. When his father died he mourned beyond the prescribed rites until his hair and beard turned white, and the court greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 後遷御史中丞、左右丞、兵部侍郎、荊揚潞長史兼采訪使，所在官吏振肅，威令甚舉，中外以為標準。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief, Left and Right Vice Directors, Vice Minister of War, and chief administrator of Jing, Yang, and Lu with concurrent touring commissioner; wherever he served, officials were shaken into order, his authority was greatly enforced, and court and countryside took him as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Vice Censor-in-Chief, left and right vice director, Vice Minister of War, and chief administrator of Jing, Yang, and Lu with touring commissioner duties. Wherever he went officials straightened up, his authority was firmly enforced, and he became a model inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部尚書、東京留守，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Revenue and Defender of the Eastern Capital, then died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Revenue and Defender of the Eastern Capital, and died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 虛心季弟 虛舟季弟虛舟，亦以舉孝廉，自御史累至戶部、司勛、左司郎中，歷荊州長史，洪、魏州刺史兼采訪使，多著能政。

translations.literal: Xuxin's youngest brother Xuzhou—Xuzhou also entered through Filial and Incorrupt recommendation; from censor he rose in succession to director in the Ministries of Revenue, Honors, and the Left Bureau; he served as chief administrator of Jing prefecture and governor of Hong and Wei with concurrent touring commissioner, and was noted for capable administration in many places.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin's youngest brother Xuzhou also entered through Filial and Incorrupt recommendation. He rose from censor to director in several ministries, served as chief administrator of Jing and as governor of Hong and Wei with touring commissioner duties, and earned a reputation for capable government.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部侍郎，終大理卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of Justice and ended as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of Justice and ended his career as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 家有禮則，父子兄弟更踐郎署，時稱「郎官家」。

translations.literal: The family had rules of propriety; father, sons, and brothers in turn served in the courtier offices, and the age called them "the Courtier family."
translations.idiomatic: The household observed strict propriety, and fathers, sons, and brothers served in turn as courtiers, earning the nickname "the Courtier clan."

sentences.zh: 韓思復韓思復，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Han Sifu—Han Sifu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sifu came from Chang'an in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 祖倫，貞觀中為左衛率，賜爵長山縣男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lun, during Zhenguan, was Commandant of the Left Guard and was granted the title Baron of Changshan county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lun served as Commandant of the Left Guard in the Zhenguan era and was enfeoffed as Baron of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 思復少襲祖爵。

translations.literal: Sifu in youth inherited his grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu inherited his grandfather's title while still young.

sentences.zh: 初為汴州司戶參軍，為政寬恕，不行杖罰。

translations.literal: At first he was revenue aide in Bian prefecture; in government he was lenient and did not impose beating punishments.
translations.idiomatic: His first post was revenue aide in Bian prefecture, where he governed leniently and never ordered beatings.

sentences.zh: 在任丁憂，家貧，鬻薪終喪制。

translations.literal: While in office he entered mourning; his household was poor, and he sold firewood to complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: While in office his father died. The family was poor, and he sold firewood to see the mourning period through.

sentences.zh: 時姚崇為夏官侍郎，知政事，深嘉嘆之，擢授司禮博士。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Chong was Vice Minister of the Ministry of War and handled state affairs; he deeply praised him and promoted him to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong, then Vice Minister of War and active in government, admired him greatly and appointed him Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: During Jinglong he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he rose to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時左散騎常侍嚴善思坐譙王重福事下制獄，有司言：「善思昔嘗任汝州刺史，素與重福交遊，召至京師，竟不言其謀逆，唯奏雲『東都有兵氣』。

translations.literal: At the time Left Regular Attendant Yan Shansi was implicated in the affair of Prince Qiao Chongfu and sent to the imperial prison; the responsible offices said: "Shansi formerly served as governor of Ru prefecture and was on familiar terms with Chongfu. Summoned to the capital, he never reported Chongfu's plot to rebel, but only memorialized that 'there is a martial aura in the eastern capital.'"
translations.idiomatic: Left Regular Attendant Yan Shansi was implicated in Prince Qiao Chongfu's case and sent to the imperial prison. The responsible offices argued: "Shansi had once been governor of Ru and was close to Chongfu. Summoned to the capital, he never reported the plot, reporting only that 'there is a martial aura in the eastern capital.'"

sentences.zh: 據狀正當匿反，請從絞刑。

translations.literal: According to the facts he should be punished for concealing rebellion; we ask that strangulation be applied.
translations.idiomatic: On the facts he had concealed treason and should be strangled.

sentences.zh: 」思復駁奏曰：「議獄緩死，列聖明規；

translations.literal: " Sifu rebutted in a memorial, saying: "To deliberate cases and defer death is the enlightened rule of successive sage emperors;
translations.idiomatic: Sifu rebutted: "Deliberating cases and deferring execution is the enlightened rule of successive emperors;

sentences.zh: 刑疑從輕，有國常典。

translations.literal: when punishment is doubtful, apply the lighter penalty—this is the constant statute of the state.
translations.idiomatic: when the law is doubtful, apply the lighter penalty—that is the standing law of the realm.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思往在先朝，屬韋氏擅內，恃寵宮掖，謀危宗社。

translations.literal: Yan Shansi in the former reign, when the Wei clan usurped power within the palace, relying on favor in the inner quarters and plotting to endanger the altars of state,
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign, when the Wei clan seized power within the palace and, relying on imperial favor, plotted against the dynasty,

sentences.zh: 善思此時遂能先覺，因詣相府有所發明，進論聖躬必登宸極。

translations.literal: was able at that time to perceive the danger first; he therefore went to the chief minister's office and made disclosures, advancing the argument that Your Sagely Person must ascend the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shansi perceived the danger early, went to the chief minister's office with revelations, and argued that Your Majesty was destined to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 雖交遊重福，蓋謀陷韋氏。

translations.literal: Although he associated with Chongfu, this was presumably to plot against the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Though he associated with Chongfu, that association was presumably aimed at bringing down the Wei faction.

sentences.zh: 及其謁見，猶不奏聞，將此行藏，即從極法。

translations.literal: Yet when he had an audience he still did not report it; to punish such conduct with the extreme penalty
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he was received in audience he still did not report the plot. To punish such conduct with death

sentences.zh: 且敕追善思，書至便發，向懷逆節，寧即奔命？

translations.literal: Moreover, when an edict summoned Shansi and he set out as soon as the letter arrived—if he had harbored treason, would he have hastened to obey?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the edict summoning Shansi arrived he set out at once. If he had harbored treason, would he have come so promptly?

sentences.zh: 一面疏網，誠合順生；

translations.literal: to loosen the net on one side truly accords with letting him live;
translations.idiomatic: To loosen the net on one side is truly to let him live;

sentences.zh: 三驅取禽，來而可宥。

translations.literal: in the three-sided hunt, game that comes forward may be spared.
translations.idiomatic: in the three-sided hunt, game that comes forward may be spared.

sentences.zh: 惟刑是恤，事合昭詳。

translations.literal: To be sparing in punishment is what the matter requires for clear deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy in punishment is what clear deliberation requires.

sentences.zh: 請付刑部集群官議定奏裁，以符慎獄。

translations.literal: I ask that the case be referred to the Ministry of Justice to assemble officials for deliberation and memorialized decision, in accord with cautious adjudication."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Ministry of Justice assemble officials to deliberate and report a decision, in keeping with careful adjudication."

sentences.zh: 」是時議者多雲善思合從原宥，有司仍執前議請誅之。

translations.literal: " At that time most of those deliberating said Shansi should be pardoned, but the responsible offices still held to their earlier opinion and asked that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those deliberating favored pardoning Shansi, but the responsible offices still pressed for execution.

sentences.zh: 思復又駁曰：「臣聞刑人於市，爵人於朝，必僉謀攸同，始行之無惑。

translations.literal: Sifu rebutted again, saying: "I have heard that punishments are carried out in the market and ennoblements in the court—only when deliberation is unanimous can action proceed without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu rebutted again: "I have heard that punishments belong in the marketplace and honors in the court—only when deliberation is unanimous can action proceed without doubt.

sentences.zh: 謹按諸司所議，嚴善思十才一入，抵罪惟輕。

translations.literal: I respectfully review the deliberations of the various offices: only one in ten argued that Yan Shansi should be punished, and the penalty proposed was the lighter one.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the deliberations of the various offices, only one in ten argued for punishment, and even then for the lighter penalty.

sentences.zh: 夫帝閽九重，塗遠千里。

translations.literal: The emperor's gate has nine layers; the road is a thousand li distant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's gate stands nine layers deep; the road to it stretches a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 故借天下之耳以聽，聽無不聰；

translations.literal: Therefore he borrows the ears of the empire to listen, and in listening nothing escapes his hearing;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he borrows the ears of the empire to listen, and nothing escapes his hearing;

sentences.zh: 借天下之目以視，視無不接。

translations.literal: he borrows the eyes of the empire to see, and in seeing nothing escapes his sight.
translations.idiomatic: he borrows the eyes of the empire to see, and nothing escapes his sight.

sentences.zh: 今群言上聞，采擇宜審，若棄多就少，臣實懼焉。

translations.literal: Now many voices have reached Your Majesty; the choice should be made with care. If the many are discarded for the few, I truly fear the consequences.
translations.idiomatic: Many voices have now reached Your Majesty, and the choice should be made with care. If the many are set aside for the few, I truly fear the consequences.

sentences.zh: 輿誦一乖，下情不達，雖欲從眾，其可及乎！

translations.literal: Once public report goes awry, sentiment below does not reach the throne; even if one wishes to follow the multitude, how can it be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Once public report goes awry, sentiment below cannot reach the throne. Even if one wishes to follow the multitude, how can that be achieved?

sentences.zh: 凡百京司，逢時之泰，列官分職，有賢有親。

translations.literal: All the capital offices, meeting a time of great peace, array officials and divide duties—some are worthy, some are kin.
translations.idiomatic: All the capital offices, in this age of great peace, divide duties among officials—some are worthy men, some are kin of the throne.

sentences.zh: 親則列籓諸王，陛下愛子；

translations.literal: Among kin are the feudatory princes, Your Majesty's beloved sons;
translations.idiomatic: Among kin are the feudatory princes, Your Majesty's beloved sons;

sentences.zh: 賢則胙茅開國，陛下名臣。

translations.literal: among the worthy are those enfeoffed with feudal states, Your Majesty's famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: among the worthy are the enfeoffed lords and Your Majesty's famed ministers.

sentences.zh: 見無禮於君，寧肯雷同不異？

translations.literal: Seeing discourtesy toward the ruler, would they willingly echo one another without difference?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing discourtesy toward the ruler, would they all echo one another without dissent?

sentences.zh: 今措詞多出，法令從輕。

translations.literal: Now the wording of many memorials favors leniency under the law."
translations.idiomatic: Now the wording of many memorials favors leniency under the law."

sentences.zh: 」上納其奏，竟免善思死，配流靜州。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his memorial and ultimately spared Shansi from death, banishing him to Jing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his memorial and spared Shansi from death, banishing him to Jing prefecture instead.

sentences.zh: 思復尋轉中書舍人，數上疏陳得失，多見納用。

translations.literal: Sifu was soon transferred to Secretariat Drafter; he repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth gains and losses, and many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was soon made Secretariat Drafter. He repeatedly memorialized on policy strengths and failings, and many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he became Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he became Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 時山東蝗蟲大起，姚崇為中書令，奏遣使分往河南、河北諸道殺蝗蟲而埋之。

translations.literal: At that time locusts rose in great numbers in Shandong; Yao Chong was Chief Minister of the Secretariat and memorialized that envoys be sent by separate routes to the circuits of Henan and Hebei to kill the locusts and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts swarmed across Shandong. Yao Chong, then Chief Minister, memorialized that envoys be sent to Henan and Hebei to kill the locusts and bury them.

sentences.zh: 思復以為蝗蟲是天災，當修德以禳之，恐非人力所能翦滅。

translations.literal: Sifu held that locusts are a heaven-sent calamity and that virtue should be cultivated to expel them; he feared they could not be exterminated by human effort.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu held that locusts were a heaven-sent calamity to be expelled through moral cultivation, not exterminated by human effort.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣聞河南、河北蝗蟲，頃日更益繁熾，經歷之處，苗稼都損。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that locusts in Henan and Hebei have recently grown still more numerous and fierce; wherever they pass, seedlings and grain are wholly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I hear that locusts in Henan and Hebei have grown fiercer still, destroying crops wherever they pass.

sentences.zh: 今漸翾飛河西，遊食至洛，使命來往，不敢昌言，山東數州，甚為惶懼。

translations.literal: Now they are gradually flying west of the river, roaming to feed as far as Luoyang; envoys come and go but dare not speak plainly, and several prefectures of Shandong are greatly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: They are now spreading west of the river and feeding as far as Luoyang. Envoys come and go but dare not speak plainly, and several Shandong prefectures are deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 且天災流行，埋瘞難盡。

translations.literal: Moreover, when heaven-sent calamity spreads, burial cannot exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: When a heaven-sent calamity spreads, burial cannot exhaust it.

sentences.zh: 望陛下悔過責躬，發使宣慰，損不急之務，召至公之人，上下同心，君臣一德，持此誠實，以答休咎。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will repent faults and examine your person, send envoys to proclaim consolation, reduce non-urgent affairs, summon the most impartial men, unite above and below in one mind and ruler and ministers in one virtue, and with this sincerity answer blessing and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will repent and examine yourself, send envoys to console the people, cut non-urgent affairs, summon the most impartial men, unite court and country in one purpose, and answer heaven's signs with sincere reform.

sentences.zh: 前後驅蝗使等，伏望總停。

translations.literal: The locust-expelling envoys sent out before and after—I humbly hope they may all be halted.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that all the locust-expelling envoys already sent out be recalled.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：『皇天無親，惟德是輔；

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'High Heaven has no favorites; it assists only virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, 'High Heaven has no favorites; it assists only virtue;

sentences.zh: 人心無親，惟惠是懷。

translations.literal: the people's hearts have no favorites; they cherish only kindness.'
translations.idiomatic: the people's hearts have no favorites; they cherish only kindness.'

sentences.zh: 』不可不收攬人心也。

translations.literal: One must not fail to win the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: You must not fail to win the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 」上深然之，出思復疏以付崇。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply approved and circulated Sifu's memorial to give it to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly approved and sent Sifu's memorial to Yao Chong.

sentences.zh: 崇乃請遣思復往山東檢蝗蟲所損之處，及還，具以實奏。

translations.literal: Chong then asked that Sifu be sent to Shandong to inspect places damaged by locusts; when he returned, he reported the facts in full.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then asked that Sifu be sent to Shandong to inspect locust damage and report the facts on his return.

sentences.zh: 崇又請令監察御史劉沼重加詳覆，沼希崇旨意，遂箠撻百姓，回改舊狀以奏之。

translations.literal: Chong also asked that Investigating Censor Liu Zhao conduct a further detailed review; Zhao, eager to please Chong's intent, beat the common people and altered the former reports in his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also ordered Investigating Censor Liu Zhao to review the reports. Eager to please Chong, Zhao beat the people and altered the earlier findings in his memorial.

sentences.zh: 由是河南數州，竟不得免。

translations.literal: Because of this several prefectures of Henan ultimately could not escape the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: As a result several Henan prefectures could not escape the disaster.

sentences.zh: 思復遂為崇所擠，出為德州刺史，轉絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Sifu was then squeezed out by Chong and sent out as governor of De prefecture, then transferred to governor of Jiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was then forced out by Chong and posted as governor of De, then transferred to Jiang.

sentences.zh: 入為黃門侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，代裴漼為御史大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, was granted the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and replaced Pei Huan as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, received the Silver-Green Tally grand master title, and replaced Pei Huan as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 思復性恬淡，好玄言，安仁體道，非紀綱之任。

translations.literal: Sifu was by nature tranquil, fond of arcane discourse, at ease in benevolence and embodying the Way—not fit for the role of enforcing discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was tranquil by nature, fond of philosophical discourse, and at ease in benevolence—not suited to the role of enforcing discipline.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died at age over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year at over seventy.

sentences.zh: 思復子 朝宗子朝宗，天寶初為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Sifu's son Chaozong—Chaozong, at the beginning of Tianbao, was Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu's son Chaozong became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao early in Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 思復曾孫 佽曾孫佽，字相之，少有文學，性尚簡淡。

translations.literal: Sifu's great-grandson Ci—Ci, style name Xiangzhi, in youth possessed literary talent and by nature valued simplicity and detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu's great-grandson Ci, styled Xiangzhi, showed literary talent in youth and valued simplicity and detachment.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累辟籓方。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to regional administrations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to serve in regional administrations.

sentences.zh: 自襄州從事征拜殿中侍御史，遷刑部員外。

translations.literal: From aide in Xiang prefecture he was summoned and appointed Palace Censor, then transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: From aide in Xiang prefecture he was summoned as Palace Censor, then promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 求為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as governor of Li prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment as governor of Li prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲滿受代，宰相牛僧孺鎮鄂渚，辟為從事，征拜刑部郎中，轉京兆少尹，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was replaced; Chief Minister Niu Sengru was stationed at Ezhou and summoned him as aide; he was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to Vice Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, Chief Minister Niu Sengru, stationed at Ezhou, summoned him as aide. He was then recalled as director in the Ministry of Justice, made Vice Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 出為桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Gui prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as Observation Commissioner of Gui.

sentences.zh: 桂管二十餘郡，州掾而下至邑長三百員，由吏部而補者什一，他皆廉吏量其才而補之。

translations.literal: Gui administered more than twenty prefectures; from prefectural aides down to district magistrates there were three hundred posts; only one in ten was filled through the Ministry of Personnel—the rest were appointed by honest officials according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui administered more than twenty prefectures with three hundred posts from prefectural aides down to district magistrates. Only one in ten was filled through the Ministry of Personnel; the rest were appointed by honest officials according to talent.

sentences.zh: 佽既至桂，吏以常所為官者數百人引謁，一吏執籍而前曰：「具員請補其闕。

translations.literal: When Ci reached Gui, clerks led several hundred men who customarily held office to an audience; one clerk came forward holding a register and said: "The full complement of posts—please fill the vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: When Ci reached Gui, clerks presented several hundred men who customarily held office. One clerk came forward with a register and said, "The posts are full—please fill the vacancies."

sentences.zh: 」佽戒曰：「在任有政者，不奪所理；

translations.literal: " Ci warned them, saying: "Those currently in office who have governed well shall not be removed from their jurisdictions;
translations.idiomatic: Ci warned them: "Those currently in office who have governed well shall keep their posts;

sentences.zh: 有過者，必繩以法。

translations.literal: those who have faults must be bound by the law.
translations.idiomatic: those at fault will be punished by law.

sentences.zh: 缺者當俟稽諸故籍，取其可者，然後補之。

translations.literal: Vacancies must await consultation of the old registers; take those who are suitable, and only then fill them."
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies must await review of the old registers; only then appoint those who are fit."

sentences.zh: 」會春衣使內官至，求賄於郵吏，三豪家因厚其資以求邑宰，佽悉諾之。

translations.literal: " When the spring-clothing envoy from the inner palace arrived and sought bribes from postal clerks, three powerful families enriched the funds to obtain district magistracies; Ci assented to all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace envoy for spring clothing arrived and sought bribes from postal clerks, three powerful families paid heavily to secure district magistracies, and Ci appeared to assent to all of them.

sentences.zh: 使去，坐以撓法，各笞其背。

translations.literal: When the envoy departed, he charged them with obstructing the law and had each flogged on the back.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy left, he charged them with obstructing the law and had each flogged.

sentences.zh: 自是豪猾斂跡，皆得清廉吏以蘇活其人。

translations.literal: From then on the powerful and cunning restrained themselves, and all obtained honest officials to revive the people.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the powerful curbed themselves, and honest officials were appointed who revived the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔置五管都監，計所費盡一境地征，不足飽其意，佽特用儉約處之，遂為定制，君子以為難。

translations.literal: Before long an edict established a general supervisor of the Five Circuits; the calculated expenses consumed an entire circuit's land tax and still did not satisfy their desires. Ci especially handled matters with frugality, and this became the fixed regulation; gentlemen regarded it as difficult to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict established a general supervisor of the Five Circuits whose expenses consumed an entire circuit's land tax and still left them unsatisfied. Ci governed with exceptional frugality, and his practice became the standard—men of principle called it a rare achievement.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，卒於官，贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he died in office; posthumously he was made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Kaicheng 2 and was posthumously honored as Vice Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 張廷珪張廷珪，河南濟源人，其先自常州徙焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinggui—Zhang Tinggui was a native of Jiyuan in Henan; his ancestors had moved there from Chang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui came from Jiyuan in Henan; his family had moved there from Chang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廷珪少以文學知名，性慷慨，有誌尚。

translations.literal: Tinggui in youth was famed for literary talent; by nature he was generous and had high aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui was famed in youth for literary talent, and he was generous by nature with high aspirations.

sentences.zh: 弱冠應制舉。

translations.literal: At age twenty he entered the special imperial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered the special imperial examination.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an reign he was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an reign he rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 則天稅天下僧尼出錢，欲於白司馬阪營建大像。

translations.literal: Empress Wu taxed monks and nuns throughout the empire to contribute funds, wishing to build a great image at White Horse Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu levied contributions from monks and nuns empire-wide to build a great image at White Horse Slope.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial in remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui submitted a memorial of remonstrance that read:

sentences.zh: 則天從其言，即停所作，仍於長生殿召見，深賞慰之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu followed his words, immediately halted the construction, and moreover summoned him to audience in the Hall of Long Life, deeply praising and comforting him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu accepted his counsel, halted construction at once, and summoned him to the Hall of Long Life to praise and comfort him warmly.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，為中書舍人，再轉洪州都督，仍為江南西道按察使。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinglong he was Secretariat Drafter, then twice transferred to Area Commander of Hong prefecture, still serving as Investigating Commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jinglong he became Secretariat Drafter, then Area Commander of Hong prefecture and Investigating Commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 開元初，入為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he returned to the capital as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時久旱，關中饑儉，下制求直諫昌言、弘益政理者。

translations.literal: At the time drought had long persisted and Guanzhong suffered famine; an edict was issued seeking forthright remonstrance and splendid words that would expand and benefit governance.
translations.idiomatic: A long drought had brought famine to Guanzhong, and an edict sought forthright counsel that would improve governance.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上疏曰：

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 再遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史蔣挺以監決杖刑稍輕，敕朝堂杖之，廷珪奏曰：「御史憲司，清望耳目之官，有犯當殺即殺，當流即流，不可決杖。

translations.literal: At the time Investigating Censor Jiang Ting, because the beating imposed in supervising a judgment was slightly light, was ordered beaten in the court hall. Tinggui memorialized, saying: "Censors are the disciplinary office, officials of pure repute who serve as the ruler's eyes and ears; if guilty they should be executed or exiled—they must not be sentenced to beating.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Jiang Ting was ordered beaten in court because the beating he supervised in a case was deemed too light. Tinggui memorialized: "Censors are the disciplinary arm of the state, the ruler's eyes and ears of pure repute. If guilty they should be executed or exiled—not beaten.

sentences.zh: 士可殺，不可辱也。

translations.literal: A gentleman may be killed but must not be humiliated."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman may be killed, but he must not be humiliated."

sentences.zh: 」時制命已行，然議者以廷珪之言為是。

translations.literal: " The order had already been carried out, but those who deliberated held Tinggui's words to be correct.
translations.idiomatic: The order had already been carried out, but deliberators held Tinggui's words to be correct.

sentences.zh: 俄坐泄禁中語，出為沔州刺史，又歷蘇、宋、魏三州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on the charge of leaking palace speech, he was sent out as governor of Mian prefecture, then served in succession as governor of Su, Song, and Wei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was charged with leaking palace secrets and posted as governor of Mian, then served in succession at Su, Song, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 入為少府監，加金紫光祿大夫，封范陽男。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Palace Domestic Service, was granted the additional title Grand Master with Gold-Purple Tally, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Director of the Palace Domestic Service, received the Gold-Purple Tally grand master title, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 四遷太子詹事，以老疾致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred four times to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired on account of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: After four appointments as Mentor of the Heir Apparent, he retired because of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，年七十余，贈工部尚書，謚曰貞穆。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died at age over seventy; posthumously he was made Minister of Public Works, with posthumous title Zhenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year at over seventy and was posthumously honored as Minister of Public Works, with the posthumous title Zhenmu.

sentences.zh: 廷珪素與陳州刺史李邕親善，屢上表薦之，邕所撰碑碣之文，必請廷珪八分書之。

translations.literal: Tinggui had long been on intimate terms with Li Yong, governor of Chen prefecture, and repeatedly submitted memorials recommending him; for stele texts composed by Yong, he invariably asked Tinggui to write them in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui had long been close to Li Yong, governor of Chen, and repeatedly recommended him. For every stele text Yong composed, he asked Tinggui to inscribe it in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 廷珪既善楷隸，甚為時人所重。

translations.literal: Since Tinggui was skilled in regular and clerical script, he was greatly esteemed by men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in regular and clerical script, he was greatly esteemed in his time.

sentences.zh: 王求禮王求禮，許州長社人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiuli—Wang Qiuli was a native of Changshe in Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli came from Changshe in Xu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則天朝為左拾遺，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: In the reign of Empress Wu he served as Left Reminder, then was transferred to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he served as Left Reminder, then became investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 性忠謇敢言，每上封彈事，無所畏避。

translations.literal: By nature he was loyal, upright, and bold in speech; whenever he submitted sealed impeachments, he feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, upright, and fearless in speech, he submitted sealed impeachments without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 時契丹李盡忠反叛，其將孫萬榮寇陷河北數州，河內王武懿宗擁兵討之，畏懦不敢進。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled; his general Sun Wanrong raided and captured several prefectures of Hebei. Wang Wuyizong of Henei led troops to suppress them but, cowardly and fearful, dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled, his general Sun Wanrong overran several Hebei prefectures. Wang Wuyizong of Henei led troops against them but, cowed by fear, dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 既而賊大掠而去，懿宗條奏滄、瀛百姓為賊詿誤者數百家，請誅之。

translations.literal: When the bandits had looted on a great scale and departed, Wuyizong submitted an itemized memorial listing several hundred households of common people in Cang and Ying who had been misled by the bandits, asking that they be executed.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels looted the region and withdrew, Wuyizong memorialized that several hundred households in Cang and Ying had been misled by the enemy and should be executed.

sentences.zh: 求禮執而劾之曰：「此詿誤之人，比無良吏教習，城池又不完固，為賊驅逼，茍徇圖全，豈素有背叛之心哉！

translations.literal: Qiuli seized on the matter and impeached him, saying: "These misled people, in recent times, had no good officials to instruct them; their walls were not secure; driven by the bandits, they sought only to preserve themselves—how could they have harbored rebellion from the first!
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli impeached him, saying: "These people were misled. They had no good officials to guide them, their defenses were weak, and the rebels drove them to save themselves—how can they be said to have harbored treason from the start?

sentences.zh: 懿宗擁強兵數十萬，聞賊將至，走保城邑，罪當誅戮。

translations.literal: Wuyizong held several hundred thousand strong troops; when he heard the bandits were coming, he fled to defend walled towns—his crime deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyizong commanded hundreds of thousands of troops, yet fled to walled towns when he heard the enemy approach—his crime deserves death.

sentences.zh: 今乃移禍於詿誤之人，豈是為臣之道？

translations.literal: Now he shifts the blame onto misled people—is this the way of a minister?
translations.idiomatic: Now he shifts blame onto the misled—is that the conduct of a minister?

sentences.zh: 請斬懿宗以謝河北百姓。

translations.literal: I ask that Wuyizong be beheaded to answer to the people of Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Wuyizong be beheaded to answer to the people of Hebei."

sentences.zh: 」懿宗大懼，則天竟降制赦之。

translations.literal: " Wuyizong was greatly afraid, and Empress Wu ultimately issued an edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyizong was terrified, and Empress Wu ultimately issued an edict pardoning the people.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷幽州，饋輓不給，左相豆盧欽望請輟京官兩月俸料以助軍，求禮謂欽望曰：「公祿厚俸優，輟之可也。

translations.literal: When the Khitan captured You prefecture and supplies could not be delivered, Left Chief Minister Dou Lu Qinwang asked that capital officials forgo two months' salary to aid the army. Qiuli said to Qinwang: "Your salary and stipend are generous; you may forgo them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan captured Youzhou and supplies failed, Left Chief Minister Dou Lu Qinwang proposed that capital officials forgo two months' salary for the army. Qiuli told him: "Your salary is generous—you may forgo it.

sentences.zh: 國家富有四海，足以儲軍國之用，何藉貧官薄俸。

translations.literal: The state is rich within the four seas and has enough to store for military and state use—why rely on the meager salaries of poor officials?
translations.idiomatic: The state is rich within the four seas and can supply military needs—why take from poor officials' thin salaries?

sentences.zh: 公此舉豈宰相法邪？

translations.literal: Is this proposal of yours the way of a chief minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this the way of a chief minister?"

sentences.zh: 」欽望作色拒之，乃奏曰：「秦、漢皆有稅算以贍軍，求禮不識大體，妄有訟辭。

translations.literal: " Qinwang changed color and rejected him, then memorialized, saying: "Qin and Han both levied taxes to supply the army; Qiuli does not understand the larger principle and rashly disputes the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang flushed with anger and rejected him, then memorialized that Qin and Han had levied taxes to supply armies and that Qiuli did not understand larger principles and rashly disputed the matter.

sentences.zh: 」求禮對曰：「秦皇、漢武稅天下，虛中以事邊，奈何使聖朝則效？

translations.literal: " Qiuli replied, saying: "The First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han taxed the empire and emptied the center to serve the frontier—how can the sage dynasty be made to imitate them?
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli replied: "The First Emperor and Emperor Wu taxed the empire and emptied the center to serve the frontier—must our sage dynasty imitate them?

sentences.zh: 不知欽望此言是大體耶！

translations.literal: Does Qinwang not know whether his words accord with the larger principle!"
translations.idiomatic: Does Qinwang not know whether his words accord with larger principles?"

sentences.zh: 」事遂不行。

translations.literal: " The matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 時三月雪，鳳閣侍郎蘇味道等以為瑞，草表將賀，求禮止之曰：「宰相調燮陰陽，而致雪降暮春，災也，安得為瑞？

translations.literal: At the time snow fell in the third month; Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Su Weidao and others took it as an auspicious sign and drafted a memorial of congratulation. Qiuli stopped them, saying: "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang, yet snow falls in late spring—this is a calamity; how can it be an auspicious sign?
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell in the third month. Vice Minister Su Weidao and others took it as an omen of good fortune and drafted a congratulatory memorial. Qiuli stopped them: "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang, yet snow falls in late spring—that is a calamity, not a blessing.

sentences.zh: 如三月雪為瑞雪，則臘月雷亦瑞雷也。

translations.literal: If snow in the third month is auspicious snow, then thunder in the twelfth month is also auspicious thunder."
translations.idiomatic: If snow in the third month is auspicious, then thunder in the twelfth month is auspicious too."

sentences.zh: 」舉朝嗤笑，以為口實。

translations.literal: " The whole court laughed and took it as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court laughed and made it a byword.

sentences.zh: 求禮竟以剛正，名位不達而卒。

translations.literal: Qiuli, because of his stern uprightness, never attained high rank and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli never rose high in rank because of his stern uprightness and died without attaining great office.

sentences.zh: 辛替否辛替否，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Xin Tifou—Xin Tifou was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifou came from the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 景龍年為左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong years he served as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he served as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時中宗置公主府官屬，安樂公主府所補尤多猥濫。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Zhongzong established official staffs for princesses' households; appointments in Princess Anle's household were especially numerous and lax.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong had established official staffs for princesses' households, and appointments in Princess Anle's household were especially numerous and improper.

sentences.zh: 又駙馬武崇訓死後，棄舊宅別造一宅，侈麗過甚。

translations.literal: Moreover, after the death of her consort Wu Chongxun, she abandoned the old residence and built another, excessively lavish.
translations.idiomatic: After her consort Wu Chongxun died, she abandoned their old residence and built another of excessive splendor.

sentences.zh: 時又盛興佛寺，百姓勞弊，帑藏為之空竭。

translations.literal: At the time Buddhist temples were also greatly promoted; the common people were worn out with labor, and the treasury was emptied for it.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist temples were also being built on a vast scale, exhausting the people and emptying the treasury.

sentences.zh: 替否上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Tifou submitted a memorial in remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou submitted a memorial of remonstrance that read:

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，安樂公主被誅。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Princess Anle was executed.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, Princess Anle was executed.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，又為金仙、玉真公主廣營二觀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, construction was again expanded on the two monasteries for the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected princesses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, construction again expanded on the two monasteries for the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected princesses.

sentences.zh: 先是，中宗時斜封受官人一切停任，凡數百千人，又有敕放令卻上。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the time of Emperor Zhongzong, all those who had received office through irregular sealed appointments had been dismissed—several hundred or a thousand in all—and there was also an edict releasing them to return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Emperor Zhongzong, all who had received office through irregular sealed appointments had been dismissed—several hundred or more—and an edict then allowed them to return.

sentences.zh: 替否時為左補闕，又上疏陳時政曰：

translations.literal: Tifou was then Left Remonstrator and again submitted a memorial setting forth current policy, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou was then Left Remonstrator and again memorialized on current policy, saying:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，睿宗嘉其公直。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong commended his fairness and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong praised his fairness and uprightness when the memorial was submitted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷為右臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Palace Censor of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Censor of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累轉潁王府長史。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan he was repeatedly transferred to chief administrator of the Prince of Ying's household.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan he rose to chief administrator of the Prince of Ying's household.

sentences.zh: 天寶初卒，年八十余。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he died at age over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Tianbao at over eighty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：夫好聞其善，惡聞其過，君人者之常情也；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The historiographer says: To love hearing of one's goodness and hate hearing of one's faults is the common disposition of rulers;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: To love hearing praise and hate hearing fault is the common disposition of rulers;

sentences.zh: 寧諂媚以取容，不逆耳以招禍，臣人者之常情也。

translations.literal: to prefer flattery to win favor rather than unwelcome words that invite disaster is the common disposition of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: to prefer flattery for favor rather than unwelcome words that invite disaster is the common disposition of ministers.

sentences.zh: 能反此者，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: To be able to reverse this—is it not excellent!
translations.idiomatic: To reverse this—is that not excellence itself?

sentences.zh: 李、薛等六君，吐忠讜之言，補朝廷之失，有犯無隱，不愧古人，有唐之良臣也。

translations.literal: The six gentlemen Li, Xue, and the others spoke loyal and forthright words, repaired the court's failings, offended without concealment, and did not disgrace the ancients—they were worthy ministers of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xue, and the other six spoke loyal and forthright words, repaired the court's failings, and offended without concealment. They did not disgrace the ancients—they were worthy ministers of Tang.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：臣之事君，有邪有正。

translations.literal: Commentary: Commentary: In how ministers serve their ruler, there is the crooked and the straight.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In how ministers serve their ruler, there is the crooked and the straight.

sentences.zh: 君之使臣，從諫則聖。

translations.literal: In how rulers employ ministers, to follow remonstrance is sagely.
translations.idiomatic: In how rulers employ ministers, to heed remonstrance is sagely.

sentences.zh: 李、薛輸忠，救人之命。

translations.literal: Li and Xue offered loyalty and saved men's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Xue offered loyalty and saved lives.

sentences.zh: 韋、韓讜言，醫國之病。

translations.literal: Wei and Han spoke bluntly and cured the state's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Han spoke bluntly and cured the state's ills.

sentences.zh: 辛、王章疏，犯顏竦聽。

translations.literal: Xin and Wang submitted forthright memorials that offended the countenance and made the ruler listen in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Wang submitted forthright memorials that made the ruler listen in awe.

sentences.zh: 張子法言，實裨時政。

translations.literal: Zhang's words accorded with law and truly benefited current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's words accorded with law and truly benefited governance.
